Why is China's market crashing and how will it affect the rest of the world?

In short, not much. It's difficult for foreigners to purchase Chinese stocks, so there is very little foreign investment in the Chinese stock market. Apparently, some Chinese were using investments in raw materials as collateral on loans to buy stocks so there may be some minor effect on commodity prices. There might be some capital flight out of China that might hit US markets and cause deflationary pressure, but I expect that effect to be small as well.

Whats more is that the government is actively trying to prop the bubble back up. They are lowering interest rates and the capital reserve requirements for banks, suspended IPOs, and is backing brokerage firms that promise to hold stocks for long periods of time. These measure, however, have done little to resolve the ~30% drop over the past month.

Supposedly Xi and Premier Li Keqiangs are implementing reforms to reduce state intervention in favor of a more open, free market. However, implementing 300 different reforms sounds like the opposite of opening up the markets.

I think the credit binge over the past several years is going to come back around and bite the Chinese market in the butt. Especially when Xi just lowered capital reserve requirements. Lets just hope their housing finance did not rely on MBS and CMBS insurance derivatives (like the U.S. housing crash).

There could be extensive impacts on commodity prices in a downward direction but this has already mostly been trending.

The market is unwinding some very high leverage, I.e the investment distortion was occuring due to the Yuan peg against the USD which has attracted global corporate interests to take advantage of "low" exchnage tradable operating costs.

This symbiosis has in turn allowed the many USD QE to run as China has been "Banking" and absorbing that USD.

The threat has always been that is the $ crashed the Chinese wealth will go with, however the Chinese figuered out simply that people will sell them tangible assets in exchange for these soon to be much less valuable USD.

This has been occuring while they prepare a Yuan Gold peg and cross exchange with the BRICS nations.

This unwinding is a step towards that, as China still uses ths USD, at the point the USD stops working for them they will dump thier USD T holdings and destory the value of the USD unless someone else wants to "Buy" it.

They will then peg or float the Yuan, these two currencies will for a time compete.
